explanation:
Mathlib has no lemma that gets `LocallyQuasiFinite` from finiteness of geometric-point fibers, meaning the sets of lifts `Spec K ⟶ X` over each `Spec K ⟶ Y` with `K` algebraically closed.

Where I looked:
- `Morphisms/QuasiFinite.lean`. Its criteria are all phrased through points or the scheme-theoretic fiber:
  - `LocallyQuasiFinite.of_finite_preimage_singleton` (finite preimage of each point) — the library's proof starts from this;
  - `locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton`, `locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isDiscrete_preimage_singleton`, `locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber`;
  - `LocallyQuasiFinite.of_fiberToSpecResidueField`, `LocallyQuasiFinite.of_injective`.
- `ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`, the only other Mathlib file that mentions `LocallyQuasiFinite`. It has only quasi-finite-locus and finite/proper results.
- Uses of `IsAlgClosed` under `AlgebraicGeometry`: none of them is about quasi-finiteness.

The library's proof needs real work on top of these: a Jacobson-space argument on the geometric fiber and an injectivity argument for sections. So it is not a one-line consequence of a single Mathlib lemma.
